headline: Commission lets tenant at 28th Spring Street hold $750 a month in escrow pending mold testing
summary: Halima Farnsworth pays $2,220 a month for a three-bedroom unit and says she has had use of only part of it since June. The landlord says repairs were finished in July and a mold test is still pending. The $750 stays in escrow until testing, and any cleaning, shows no mold and the health inspector reports the same. The commission also adopted its rules of procedure.
decisions: Continued the Tussman and St. Germain case to the December 16 meeting, until the parties sign their agreement.
Accepted the November 17, 2026 health notice of violation as evidence in the case.
Failed: a motion to hold $120 a month in escrow pending testing and a cleaning report.
Approved holding $750 a month in escrow pending mold testing.
Adopted the commission's rules of procedure.
discussion: Mold at 28th Spring Street: The tenant said visible mold and water on a bare floor have kept her from using part of her unit since June. The landlord said repairs were completed by July 19 and that an environmental company's test would take 24 hours to return.

Rent reduction request: The tenant asked for a rent reduction. Members said the commission can only allow, deny, or phase in a rent increase or hold rent in escrow, and the city ordinance does not allow a rent reduction.
Rent increase: The landlord proposed a $60 rent increase, which the tenant has been paying. The landlord said it did not think going back to the earlier rent made sense.
New complaint application: The new form is longer and asks for more information. Members said it should weed out frivolous complaints, and it will be posted on the website.
